feedback: No race has been run on this platform yet, so there is no earlier evidence about this geometry. The controller in this package is a first baseline, so the Builder should not read any result into it. Next race, if line_loss_events are high on the slalom and max_error is large there, the sensing span is the likely limit: widen sensor x-positions (for example to ±0.04 m) before changing the wheel track. If the race completes with low rms_error but completion_time is above about 2.5 s, the drivetrain is the limit: try a smaller wheel_track (0.10 m) or lower mass (0.6 kg) to raise turn rate. If steering_oscillation is high on the s-bend or oval, keep sensor y at 0.05 m and try a shorter forward lead (y = 0.03 m) to reduce phase lag, since a longer lead can amplify oscillation at speed. The integration questions in the Builder's request (sensor span saturation, lead lag, mass and track turn authority) are not yet answered by any measurement; they should be answered from the first race's telemetry.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events are high: widen the sensor span from 0.06 m to 0.08 m by setting sensor x-positions to -0.04, -0.02, 0.0, 0.02, 0.04 (sensor_size stays 0.012). Hypothesis from the Builder's learning item (1); no race data yet.

If completion_time is above about 2.5 s with low rms_error: reduce wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m and mass from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg to raise turn rate. Based on the Builder's baseline hypothesis (3); no race data yet.
If steering_oscillation is high on the s-bend or oval: move sensor y from 0.05 m to 0.03 m to reduce forward lead and phase lag. Based on the Builder's baseline hypothesis (2); no race data yet.
